name: Alberton Ozone
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; the address is provisional and the exact property has not been verified.
summary: The Alberton Ozone in Fussell Place opened on 25 August 1924 as the second picture house built for South Australia's Ozone circuit. It converted to sound films at Christmas 1930, passed to Hoyts in 1951 and was sold in 1964 to become a supermarket.

sources.title: CAARP (Cinema and Audience Research Project): Ozone, Alberton

name: Naracoorte Institute
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; no address is shown because it has not been verified.
summary: The Naracoorte Institute has screened films under several names, including Austral Pictures and the Landmark Cinema, and has also been known as the Town Hall.

sources.title: CAThS: South Australian cinema and theatre venues list

name: Starlight Drive-in
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; no address is shown because it has not been verified.
summary: The Starlight Drive-in at Watson operated from 1957 until 1993, when the site was redeveloped for motel accommodation. Its entrance sign survives and is on the ACT Heritage Register; it was conserved and reinstated close to its original position in 2015.

sources.title: ArchivesACT: Sundown and Starlight, Canberra's drive-in theatres (Find of the Month, December 2022)
ACT Legislation Register: Heritage (Further Registration Decision for the Starlight Drive-In Theatre Sign, Watson) Notice 2016, NI2016-173

notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; the address is provisional and the exact property has not been verified.
summary: Palace Electric Cinema is a cinema at 2 Phillip Law Street, Canberra, run by Palace Cinemas. Its operator listed it at this address when checked in November 2026.

name: Cygnet Cinema (Como Theatre)
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; the address is provisional and the exact property has not been verified.
summary: The Cygnet Cinema, first known as the Como Theatre, opened at 16 Preston Street, Como, on 4 March 1938. It has been on Western Australia's State Register of Heritage Places since 1995.

sources.title: inHerit (Heritage Council of WA): Cygnet Cinema, Place 02404

name: Central 70 Drive-in
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; no address is shown because it has not been verified.
summary: The Central 70 Drive-in at Albany opened on 26 December 1964. It closed in early 1983, soon after changing hands, and the land was later subdivided for industry.

sources.title: Pictures in Motion (AMMPT Western Region): Central 70 Drive-In, Albany

name: Salon Lumière
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; the address is provisional and the exact property has not been verified.
summary: The Salon Lumière at 237 Pitt Street, Sydney, showed films with the Lumière Cinématographe in 1896. The National Film and Sound Archive describes it as Australia's first cinema. After it closed, a new tenant reopened the rooms as the Salon Cinématographe.

sources.title: National Film and Sound Archive: Salon Lumière, Australia's first cinema

name: Temperance Hall (Everybody's Pictures; Empire)
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; no address is shown because it has not been verified.
summary: Penrith's Temperance Hall hosted film screenings from 1903 and became a permanent picture theatre, Everybody's Pictures, in 1918. It was renamed the Empire in 1922 and destroyed by fire the following year.

sources.title: Nepean District Historical Society Bulletin 56 (April 2023): Penrith Goes to the Movies, compiled by Steve Maggs

name: Nepean Open-Air
notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; no address is shown because it has not been verified.
summary: The Nepean began as an open-air picture show on a vacant block in Penrith on 9 March 1911, with seats for about 1,000 people and screenings in summer only. Its owners later converted neighbouring buildings into the indoor Nepean Theatre.

sources.title: Nepean District Historical Society Bulletin 56 (April 2023): Penrith Goes to the Movies, compiled by Steve Maggs

notice: Archive listing. The name and place are approved by an editor; the address is provisional and the exact property has not been verified.
summary: Coffs City Centre Cinema 3 opened in Vernon Street, Coffs Harbour, beside the Cinema Walk Arcade on 5 May 1988 and closed on 30 October 2002. The building is now used for shops and offices.

summary: Launceston's Plaza Theatre began as the Academy of Music, which became a picture house and was remodelled as the Plaza in 1937. The source gives the building's years of use as 1886 to 1964.

summary: The Mount Morgan School of Arts opened in 1924, replacing earlier halls lost to fire, and has been used for films as well as balls and stage shows since then. It reopened after refurbishment in 2011.
